East has some irregular, angled plates, but north shows neat symmetric overlapping bands and scutes. 3) Scar-tissue surface: WEAK. The plates are smooth, pitted bone-grey; red, slightly fibrous tissue shows only in the seams, with no puckered, seared or keloid surface. 4) Slab as a separate mass on top of the legs: ABSENT. The armour wraps continuously down the legs and over the head, which reads as a shelled animal with limbs and head coming out of its shell.

STYLE.seen: Painterly and realistic: textured plates, a clean dark outline, not cute, no glossy eyes.

OURS.seen: Original creature art installed under RimMandrake/Contagion. Nothing matches a vanilla or donor animal.

ALPHA.seen: Clean cut-out on every facing. No ground patch, shadow or halo.

SCALE.seen: About a cell long and below the human's height: a mid-sized beast, which fits an unsized 'armoured slab on legs' (drawSize 1.15).

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px it reads as a pale clawed lump that stands apart from the brown ground. The detail is lost, but the silhouette holds.

findings.seen: The body is a tall dome in south and north and a humped arch in east, standing high on its legs.
findings.quote: Body is a low, flat slab rather than a domed shell or rounded banded carapace
findings.fix: Make the body a low, broad, flat-topped slab only a little taller than the legs beneath it, wide and thick like a heavy flagstone, with a flat top line on south, east and north.

findings.seen: North shows neat, symmetric, regularly overlapping scale rows down a central ridge and a banded segmented tail: classic pangolin imbrication.
findings.quote: Armour plates fused wrong: irregular, misaligned and asymmetric, not neat overlapping bands or scutes
findings.fix: Draw the armour as a few large, irregular, asymmetric plates fused together at wrong angles, with gaps, ridged weld seams and overlaps that differ from left to right on every facing, including the rear and tail.

findings.seen: The plates are smooth, pitted, bone-grey or stone-like. Red fibrous tissue shows only in the seams, and no surface reads as puckered, seared or keloid scar.

findings.fix: Make the plate surfaces themselves look like thick seared scar tissue: glossy keloid ridges, puckered and stretched pink-white skin, cracked char and blistered edges across the whole slab, not only in the seams.

findings.seen: The armour wraps continuously over the head and down every leg to the claws, so it reads as a shelled animal with a head and limbs coming out of its shell.

findings.fix: Show the slab as one distinct mass resting on top of four bare, sinewy legs, with a clear break and exposed underside between the slab and the legs, and no shell-encased head poking out.

findings.seen: The overall read is a pangolin or armadillo: a domed imbricated scaly body, a banded tapering tail and a lowered head under the scales.
findings.quote: Invented creatures and plants read as ALIEN, never as a recoloured Earth species.
findings.fix: Make the silhouette alien: a flat, uneven scar-slab on separate legs with no pangolin-style tail bands or dome, so that no Earth animal comes to mind.

findings.seen: The defining 'low armoured slab of scar tissue' is not delivered: the body is high-domed, and the armour reads as bone or stone plates.
findings.quote: The defining feature the description names ... is visible and legible.
findings.fix: The creature is a low armoured slab of fused, seared scar tissue carried on legs, legible as a slab at a glance on every facing.

findings.seen: Measured spread is 19%. South (166 px) is visibly taller and wider than north (148 px), with a higher dome and wider leg splay, though both views are equally deep.
findings.quote: it needs the treatment that makes the different facings the same size.
findings.fix: Scale the south and north facings so that body width and height match each other and the east view's body height.

findings.seen: East's plates are large and irregular, while north's are small, regular, evenly stacked rows, so the armour pattern differs between the views.
findings.quote: facings disagree on anatomy/palette
findings.fix: Use the same large irregular plate layout on every facing, so the plates seen on east appear foreshortened on north and south.

findings.seen: At 32 px/cell it is a small pale grey-red lump with claws, and the slab or plate idea disappears.

The armour is a few large, irregular, asymmetric plates fused together at wrong angles, with gaps, ridged weld seams and overlaps that differ left to right on every view, including the rear.

The plate surfaces themselves are thick seared scar tissue: glossy keloid ridges, puckered and stretched pink-white skin, cracked char and blistered edges across the whole slab, with raw red tissue in the seams.

The slab is one distinct mass resting on top of four bare, sinewy, unarmoured legs, with a clear gap and exposed dark underside between slab and legs; the head is a small bare-skinned lump that is not encased by the slab.
The silhouette is alien: a flat, uneven scar-slab on separate thin legs, with a short stubby rear edge of the slab and no tapering banded tail, so no Earth animal comes to mind.
The creature reads at a glance as a low armoured slab of fused, seared scar tissue carried on legs, on every view.
All three views share the same slab width, slab height and leg length as the side view; the front and rear views show the same slab foreshortened, not larger.
The same large irregular plate layout appears on every view: the plates seen from the side are foreshortened in the front and rear views, with the same seams and the same fused-wrong angles.

painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, clean dark outline

request.prompt: A single RimWorld creature sprite, the scaldhide, on a transparent background, in painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, with a clean dark outline. The scaldhide is a low armoured slab of scar tissue carried on four legs: it walks out into the killing light and eats what it finds already cooked. The body is a low, broad, flat-topped slab only a little taller than the legs beneath it, wide and thick like a heavy flagstone, with a flat top line on the front, side and rear views. The slab is one distinct mass resting on top of four bare, sinewy, unarmoured legs, with a clear gap and exposed dark underside between slab and legs. The armour is a few large, irregular, asymmetric plates fused together at wrong angles, with gaps, ridged weld seams and overlaps that differ left to right on every view, including the rear. The plate surfaces themselves are thick seared scar tissue: glossy keloid ridges, puckered and stretched pink-white skin, cracked char and blistered edges across the whole slab, with raw red tissue in the seams. The head is a small bare-skinned lump at the front, not encased by the slab; in the front view its eyes face the viewer, and in the rear view, seen from behind, the head is hidden and the back edge of the slab and the haunches show, with a short stubby slab edge and no tapering banded tail. The silhouette is alien, a flat uneven scar-slab on separate thin legs, so no Earth animal comes to mind. Palette: scorched red-pink, pale scar-white, char brown and near-black seams. Reference: none; build the body from this description. The same slab width, slab height, leg length and large irregular plate layout appear on every view, with the plates seen from the side foreshortened in the front and rear views, and the front and rear views match the side view in body height and width.
